title: Operating System Process State Transition Diagram
prompt: Generate a state transition diagram of Operating System process states (New, Ready, Running, Waiting, Terminated).
mermaid_code:
stateDiagram-v2

[New]--[Allocate Resources]-->[Ready]
[Ready]--[Scheduling]-->[Running]
[Running]--[I/O Request]-->[Waiting]
[Waiting]--[Resource Available]-->[Ready]
[Ready]--[Scheduling]-->[Running]
[Running]--[Completion]-->[Terminated]
[Terminated]--[Cleanup]-->[Closed]
[Waiting]--[Timeout]-->[Ready]
[Ready]--[Scheduling]-->[Running]
[Running]--[I/O Request]-->[Waiting]
[Waiting]--[Resource Available]-->[Ready]
[Ready]--[Scheduling]-->[Running]
[Running]--[Completion]-->[Terminated]
[Terminated]--[Cleanup]-->[Closed]
explanation: This diagram illustrates the state transitions of an operating system process lifecycle. The states are: New, Ready, Running, Waiting, and Terminated. The transitions reflect how a process moves through these states based on system operations and resource availability. The diagram shows the natural progression of a process from creation to termination, with specific transitions for resource allocation, scheduling, and waiting for I/O or other resources.
